customManagers.description: OpenTofu provider pins for the CDK Terrain stacks. A bump here is half of an upgrade: Mend-hosted Renovate cannot run post-upgrade commands, so someone runs bun run --cwd packages/homelab-cdktn providers:refresh on the branch to move the lock files, bindings and synthesized JSON. CI fails until that is done.
Update the structured homelab version catalog

Hinted version pins. Grammar: a comment `renovate: datasource=X depName=Y [packageName=P] [registryUrl=U] [versioning=V] [extractVersion=RE]` directly above `ARG|ENV NAME=VALUE`, `NAME="VALUE"`, `NAME = "VALUE"` or `[export] const NAME = "VALUE"`. An `ARG *_COMMIT=<sha>` on the next line is that version's commit and moves with it. `datasource=git-refs depName=Y packageName=<repo URL> ref=HEAD|branch=<name>` above `ARG|ENV NAME=<sha>` follows a branch head. Checksum ARGs beside a pin are NOT updated: Mend-hosted Renovate cannot run post-upgrade commands, so such a bump is half an upgrade; a human refreshes the companion named in the PR body and the image build or pin check fails until then. scripts/checks/deps/check-renovate-hints.ts fails on any hint this grammar does not extract.
macOS cross-compiler Swift base image, kept in sync across the structured SDK catalog and Dockerfile default
Talos factory installer image — track the trailing :vX.Y.Z (schematic hash regenerated by update-image-id.ts)
pokeemerald-wasm source pin — track ottohg master HEAD in the language-neutral upstream manifest and Dockerfile build stage
redlib source pin — track upstream main HEAD for the image build (ARG REDLIB_SOURCE_REF)

Pins in .mise.toml that Renovate's native mise manager cannot resolve. Amazon Corretto: the native mise/java datasource cannot resolve the corretto-X.Y.Z.B.R build string, so track corretto/corretto-25 GitHub release tags (e.g. 25.0.4.7.1) directly. .NET SDK: native mise reports dotnet as an unsupported datasource, so track the dotnet-version datasource that global.json already uses. Every other tool in the file is tracked natively and carries no hint.

The Storm Modrinth plugin URLs, in the production manifest and every mirror of it. The whole file URL is the version (custom.modrinth); the registry URL limits candidates to releases for the Paper family in server/plugins.json (scripts/renovate-config.test.ts). A bump is half an upgrade: Renovate moves only the URL, and a human fills version, sha256 and file (Modrinth publishes no SHA-256).
The Storm BlueMap pin. One match spans the whole plugins.json entry, so the version, the release URL and the file name move together; only sha256 stays manual.
Mirrors of the version catalog's itzg/minecraft-server pin in the Minecraft harness and the Storm e2e CI lane (tag and digest).

SwiftLint version in the CI producer's frozen inputs (ci/scripts/swiftlint/validate-inputs.py requires it to equal the catalog). Half upgrade: the source revision and archive checksum beside it stay manual.

SwiftLint builder image in the CI producer's frozen inputs (ci/scripts/swiftlint/validate-inputs.py requires it to equal the catalog and the ci-image ARG SWIFTLINT_BUILDER_IMAGE, which the native dockerfile manager reads).

Storybook ships its core, framework and addons as one release train; a partial bump leaves the builder and addons on mismatched internal APIs, so they update together in one PR.

Keep react, react-dom and their @types in lockstep. React 19 throws 'Incompatible React versions' at runtime when react and react-dom differ, so they must always bump together in one PR to the same resolved version. Enforced by scripts/checks/deps/check-react-version-sync.ts.

Ignore architecture-specific Plex tags (armhf, arm64)

Track modern qBittorrent app tags with single-digit majors 4-9. Historical Ubuntu tags use two-digit majors such as 14 and 20; Docker version normalization removes their zero-padded minor, so checking the minor alone cannot reject those stale images.

sherpa-onnx 1.13.2-1.13.4 miss KWS/streaming-ASR detections on FEAT_SME arm64 (bundled onnxruntime 1.27.0 Conv bug, k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx#3791/#3776). Fixed upstream via ORT 1.27.1 in k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx#3831 (macOS) and #3850 (Linux aarch64/Android), both merged before the 1.13.5 release. allowedVersions skips only the broken window; the functional startup smoke in packages/streambot/src/voice/local-models.ts is the upgrade gate before bumping past the current 1.13.1 pin.

velero-plugin-for-aws 1.14.1-1.14.2 send an empty x-amz-tagging header on every PutObject, which Cloudflare R2 rejects with 501 NotImplemented, failing all Velero backup-metadata uploads (PR #1307 deployed it 2026-06-21 → every backup Failed since, plus orphaned ZFS/R2 data: incidents #5860 and #5849). The upstream guard (velero-io/velero-plugin-for-aws#299) landed in v1.14.3, confirmed by source inspection (buildPutObjectInput only sets Tagging when configured); v1.14.2 does not have it. allowedVersions skips only the broken window; verify against R2 before bumping past the current v1.14.0 pin.

Renovate's gradle manager extracts the jacoco and pmd Gradle tool versions as deps whose `version` variable resolves to the plugin's own version in gradle.properties, proposing nonsense bumps such as jacoco 0.8.16 that would rewrite it. The real pins live in libs.versions.toml, tracked through the jacoco-agent and pmd-java catalog libraries.
Fabric API versions end in +<minecraft version>; stay on the build for the Minecraft version in client-minecraft (libs.versions.toml) and move both by hand together.
Hold Renovate's built-in @tsconfig/node24 to @tsconfig/node26 replacement: Node 26 adoption is tracked in Tracker AI-871 and .mise.toml pins node 24.
Keep @tsconfig/node-lts below node26 until Tracker AI-871 moves Node past the node 24 pin in .mise.toml.

The deb and git-refs datasources carry no release timestamps. Under the strict 30-day release-age gate an update without a timestamp stays pending forever, so these skip the gate.

GrimAC resolves from a Modrinth Ivy repository (packages/the-storm/plugin/settings.gradle.kts), not Maven Central; the Maven lookup can only fail or be rate limited. The custom.modrinth manager tracks it from the Storm server manifest instead, and the GrimAC prBodyNotes name these Gradle pins.
The Storm client's Minecraft version follows the Paper line by hand. Fabric Loom resolves com.mojang:minecraft itself; it has no Maven release metadata to look up.
Half upgrade: The Storm's Modrinth plugins are hash-pinned, and Modrinth publishes no SHA-256, so Renovate moves only each copy of the URL.
prBodyNotes: **Half upgrade.** Renovate moved only the download URL. In `packages/the-storm/server/plugins.json`, set this plugin's `version`, `file` and `sha256` (`curl -fsSL <url> | sha256sum`) to the new build, and copy `version` and `sha256` to the same plugin in `packages/the-storm/tests/e2e/harness/pins.ts` and `packages/mc-harness/src/pins.ts`. `packages/the-storm/tests/pins.test.ts` fails until `version` and `file` match the URL and every copy agrees; the image build (`server/fetch.sh`) fails until `sha256` matches.

packageRules.description: ci/scripts/swiftlint/validate-inputs.py requires the catalog and the CI producer's pins.json to name the same SwiftLint release. Half upgrade: the source revision and archive checksum are manual.
prBodyNotes: **Half upgrade.** In `ci/scripts/swiftlint/pins.json`, set `sourceRevision` to the commit tag {{{newValue}}} names, point `sourceArchive` at it, and set `sourceArchiveSHA256` to that archive's SHA-256. Upgrades also require the configured-rule and SourceKit canaries.

packageRules.description: ci/scripts/swiftlint/validate-inputs.py requires the catalog, the CI producer's pins.json and the ci-image ARG SWIFTLINT_BUILDER_IMAGE to name the same Swift builder image. Half upgrade: the Swift license URLs and checksums are manual.
prBodyNotes: **Half upgrade.** If the Swift release changed, point both `runtimeLicenses` URLs in `ci/scripts/swiftlint/pins.json` at the new `swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE` tag and refresh their `sha256`.

packageRules.description: The catalog's ffsubsync pin and the hash-locked media subtitle requirements move together. Half upgrade: the version is also part of the subtitle receipt identities.
prBodyNotes: **Half upgrade.** Update the `ffsubsync-<version>` engine and detector literals in `packages/media/src` and the version assertion in `packages/temporal/Dockerfile`, and refresh the transitive hashes in `packages/media/scripts/subtitle-requirements.txt`. Then run the speech coverage and timing tests.
